title: session-aware deferred cutover with telemetry reconciliation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds session-aware deferred-cutover mode to the rollout controller: holds active-session traffic on the current model variant and performs cutover only after session drain + telemetry reconciliation. Includes opt-in config, observability dashboards, and a replayable rollback snapshot.
description:
Summary: Adds a new rollout mode 'session-aware-deferred-cutover' to the rollout controller which delays model cutover for user sessions that have active KV/stream state until they finish or a configurable timeout elapses. The controller performs a short telemetry reconciliation step before finishing the cutover: it compares pre-cutover shadow traffic signals (latency/error distributions, core eval metrics) with live production signals to detect silent regressions and abort/cancel the cutover if anomalies exceed thresholds. Motivation: We observed customer incidents where in-session state (long chat sessions / streaming contexts) would experience partial degradation after rapid swaps due to cold KV caches and session-affine heuristics. Existing canary and shadow modes focused on aggregate metrics and failed to guarantee session continuity. This PR implements an opt-in defensive mode for teams that need session-consistent cutovers with minimal runtime complexity.

What changed (high-level): - rollout/controller: new strategy 'SessionDeferredCutover' with state machine (PENDING -> QUIESCING_SESSIONS -> RECONCILING -> COMMIT/ABORT). - routing: small router changes to annotate requests with session-affinity metadata and TTL when applicable. - telemetry: reconciliation comparator that consumes short-window histograms from the metrics pipeline (latency, 2xx/4xx/5xx, model token length distributions). - snapshotting: on-prepare we capture a lightweight rollout snapshot (routing map + sample request hashes) to support deterministic rollback and replay. - console/ui: expose the new mode in the rollout policy dropdown and show reconciliation diffs in the rollout timeline. - docs: rollout-mode.md describes configuration knobs and playbook. - e2e tests + unit tests + simulation harness update.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (Linear ENG-3421) reviewed - [x] Unit tests for controller state transitions - [x] e2e simulation with synthetic sessions - [x] Backwards-compatible (default mode is unchanged) - [x] Console flag gated and feature-flagged rollout for GA after opt-in

Commits (summary): - 4f3c2b0: controller: add SessionDeferredCutover state machine and configuration layer - 9b21a7f: router: add session-affinity annotation and drain TTL handshake - a6d3f4e: telemetry: reconciliation comparator and histogram diff helper - d1e72ff: api: rollout CRUD schema extension + validation - 7c8b0ad: console: UI for reconciliation diff and manual abort - faf3b9e: tests: simulation scenarios for session drain and abort flows

Files changed (high-level): - rollout/controller/strategy_session_deferred.go (new, ~420 lines) - routing/router_session_affinity.go (mod) - telemetry/reconciler.go (new) - api/v1/rollouts.proto (mod) - console/src/components/RolloutTimeline/ReconciliationView.tsx (mod) - docs/rollout-modes/SESSION_DEFERRED.md (new) - tests/e2e/session_deferred_simulation.yaml (new) - infra/ci/rollout_integration_test.yml (mod)

Snippet (policy example):

rolloutPolicy:
  mode: SESSION_DEFERRED
  sessionDrainTimeout: 30s
  reconWindow: 30s
  reconThresholds:
    latency_p95_pct: 10  # percent increase tolerated
    error_rate_abs: 0.005

Behavior notes: - When enabled, the controller creates a mirrored shadow lane while gradually directing new sessions to the candidate variant only once the shadow baseline satisfies similarity constraints. Existing active sessions on the incumbent are quiesced; their routing is preserved until they end or the sessionDrainTimeout expires. - After session quiesce, the controller triggers a reconWindow (default 30s) where it compares the candidate's shadow telemetry against the incumbent's production telemetry. If the reconciliation comparator finds an anomaly above any reconThreshold, the controller aborts the cutover and can optionally promote the candidate to a longer shadow for further evaluation. - Rollback snapshot includes routing map version and sample request hashes; the rollback path uses the snapshot to ensure deterministic session routing during revert.

Review conversation (selected): - Lena Ortiz (2026-02-11): "Great approach. A few comments: (1) can we make the reconWindow configurable per-metric? (2) make sure the snapshot avoids PII (sample request hashes ok)." -> Maya Chen: "(1) added reconThresholds block so teams may tune per-metric thresholds; reconWindow left global for now to keep state transitions simple. We can follow up with per-metric windows in a follow-up. (2) snapshots are salted hashes; updated doc note and test to assert no plain text is kept." - Ravi Kapoor (2026-02-13): "Safety: add a configurable maximum consecutive aborts to avoid flip-flopping during noisy periods." -> Maya Chen: "Added maxConsecutiveAborts (defaults to 2) and instrumentation for abort_count metric." - Owen Li (2026-02-15): "CI flakes in the e2e harness: simulated session TTLs causing test timeouts. Suggest shortening synthetic session durations and add a fast-path unit test for transition logic." -> Maya Chen: "Adjusted tests and added a fast-path unit that exercises the QUIESCING_SESSIONS -> RECONCILING -> COMMIT path without wall-clock waits. CI now passes."

CI and gating: - Integration tests: rollout integration suite (passes) - Lint: pass - Typechecks: pass - Load tests: lightweight smoke (passes) - One flaky test in internal simulation was adjusted and stabilized

Backward compatibility and migration: - Default rollout mode remains as before; SessionDeferredCutover is opt-in via rolloutPolicy.mode or feature flag. - API change: rollout protobuf adds enum value; we follow forward/backwards compatibility guidelines (unknown enum handled safely on older controllers). - No database schema changes; snapshots are stored as compressed metadata blobs.

Operational playbook (summary): - To enable: set rolloutPolicy.mode=SESSION_DEFERRED on target rollout + optionally set sessionDrainTimeout and reconThresholds. - Monitor: rollout.timeline, recon_diff charts, abort_count and session_drain_active metrics. - Abort path: controller will move to ABORT state and emit snapshot for replay. Manual abort from console is supported. - Rollback: supported via snapshot ID; run the replay tool to rehydrate routing and then perform standard rollback.

Why this is different from existing modes: Unlike plain shadow/canary which evaluate aggregate signals, this mode understands session boundaries and preserves session affinity to avoid mid-session tokenization/kv cache artifacts. The telemetry reconciliation step explicitly measures short-window distribution similarity post-quiesce, reducing the chance of silent regressions that only appear in long sessions.

Performance considerations: - Adds minor routing annotation overhead (~0.2% increase in per-request header size). - Controller keeps additional short-lived state per rollout; memory impact is bounded by active rollout count. - Telemetry comparator queries are short-window histograms (default 30s) sampled at low cardinality to limit ingestion costs.

Notes and follow-ups: - Follow-up to add per-metric recon windows and automated escalation to longer shadow if recon fails but abort_count remains near threshold. - Consider exposing a dry-run reconciliation mode in the console for safety reviews.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged into main on 2026-02-18 after approvals from Lena and Ravi. Changelog entry added to the release notes under 'Rollout features'.
